title: Grade 5 Science — Tue, May 19
description: Food Web & Ecosystem — Last Week Day 2
subject: science

questions.question: A food chain starts with:
questions.explanation: All food chains start with producers (green plants) that make their own food via photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which correctly shows a food chain?
questions.explanation: Energy flows from producer to consumer: Grass → Rabbit → Fox.

questions.question: Animals that eat only plants are called:
questions.explanation: Herbivores eat only plant material. Examples: cow, deer, rabbit.

questions.question: Decomposers are important because they:
options: Break down dead organisms and return nutrients to soil
questions.explanation: Decomposers (fungi, bacteria) break down dead matter and recycle nutrients back into the ecosystem.

questions.question: What happens if all producers in an ecosystem disappear?
questions.explanation: Without producers, herbivores starve, then carnivores have no prey — the entire food chain collapses.

questions.question: A food web is different from a food chain because:
options: It shows many interconnected food chains
questions.explanation: A food web shows multiple interconnected food chains — it's more realistic than a single chain.

questions.question: Which is a second-order consumer in: Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake?
questions.explanation: Frog eats grasshopper (first consumer). Frog is the second-order consumer.

questions.question: The relationship between a lion and zebra is:
questions.explanation: The lion (predator) hunts and eats the zebra (prey) — this is predation.

questions.question: Sunlight → Grass → Deer → Tiger. How many trophic levels are there?
Mushrooms growing on a dead log are examples of:
questions.explanation: Mushrooms (fungi) are decomposers — they break down dead organic matter.

questions.question: What is meant by 'biodiversity'?
options: Variety of living organisms in an area
questions.explanation: Biodiversity refers to the variety of all living organisms — plants, animals, fungi, microbes — in an area.

questions.question: Which human activity MOST damages ecosystems?
questions.explanation: Deforestation destroys habitats, reduces biodiversity, and disrupts food chains.

questions.question: Bears eat both plants and animals. They are:
questions.explanation: Omnivores eat both plants and animals. Bears eat berries, fish, and other animals.

questions.question: Energy from the sun is captured by plants through:
questions.explanation: Plants capture solar energy through photosynthesis, converting CO₂ and water into glucose.

questions.question: What does 'endangered species' mean?
options: A species that is very common
A species at risk of extinction
questions.explanation: An endangered species is at high risk of becoming extinct if its situation does not improve.
